observations: Two large black animal-like forms dominate the upper half, each marked with red X shapes over circular eye areas and outlined in yellow and neon lines against a cream and blue background.
A dense lower band of black and white interlocking rectangular shapes sits beneath a yellow zigzag border, with red and purple loose scribble lines looping across the bottom third.
On the right edge, a bold yellow spiral and a second concentric-ring shape anchor the composition, while scattered yellow angular fragments and a red horizontal slash cross the upper right corner.
reading: Two black figures face outward, their eyes crossed out in red, their outlines buzzing with yellow and neon. The lower zone locks into a maze of white rectangles that reads as both contained and restless. Red X marks and tooth-row forms carry a charged, unsettled feeling. The spiral on the right edge holds steady against the surrounding scatter, offering a single point of stillness.
contextAngle: The owned subset holds two works sharing the title nnotb #249, neighbors in title order but not confirmed creation order. The collector links nnxyz's looping line patterns to scrimshaw's repeat marks, a visual quality rather than an artist statement.

connections.reason: The two works share nearly the entire composition and color, but this primary image shows a plain lower-right signature area, while the comparison carries additional yellow marks over that same zone — a narrow but visible distinction between two same-title objects.

Both works use crown marks, red X shapes on circular eye forms, and a visible tooth row, but nnotb #250 places these on a pale ground with orange-glowing eyes, sharpening the contrast with this work's black-filled forms.

lookingQuestion: Where does your eye settle first — on the red X marks, the yellow spiral, or the white rectangle maze — and what does that path tell you about how the forms compete for attention?
ambiguities: The two nnotb #249 images share nearly the full composition; the confirmed visible difference is the presence of yellow marks over the lower-right signature in the comparison image and their absence in this primary image.
The animal-like forms could be read as cats, dogs, or invented creatures; no title or metadata confirms the subject, so the description stays with observable shape.
